newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Volatile PGMs show no sign of calming.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Volatile PGMs show no sign of calming.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Severe volatility in the platinum group metals (PGMs) shows no sign of slowing, with spot platinum prices indicated at seven-year highs on Friday, dealers said.
Gold and silver are finally benefitting from the PGM price hikes, but only slightly.

PLATINUM - Prices surged a spectacular $50 following the London gold close to be indicated at a high $480/$510 in early European trading, underscoring the severe supply tightness and volatility of the PGMs.

Technical indicators were of little use at this point in predicting the next price movement in platinum and palladium because traders needing to cover short positions would be forced to buy spot at very high prices, dealers said.
Platinum was last indicated at $470.00/$500.00, versus $446.60/$456.60 at Thursday's New York close.
PALLADIUM - Similarly palladium will remain in stormy waters pending resumption of Russian exports, dealers said.

The market was anxiously watching out for defaults in the market, despite an emergency meeting of market makers on Thursday which said there had been none so far. Prices were bid at $235.00, versus $213.50/$223.50 at the New York close on Thursday.
GOLD - PGM strength has trickled into the gold market, although prices have been reluctant to break out of a narrow range, dealers noted.
On the downside the $339.20 low of Thursday appears to be solid support, but a breach of the recent $347.00 high could be troublesome barring strong speculative interest, a dealer said.
Prices were last indicated at $344.50/$345.50, up $1.40 from the late finish.

SILVER - Prices broke above the previous resistance of $4.85 and then $4.92 on Friday morning, suggesting further strength against a background of gently uptrending near-term indicators, dealers said.
A key level would at $5.00.
Support is seen at the 10-day moving average of $4.75.
Silver was last quoted at $4.89/$4.91, up nine cents from the New York close.
--Lida Poletz, London newsroom +44 171 542 2936
